text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- 11 opposition MPs suggested a vote of no-confidence in Welfare Minister Vladimirs Makarovs. The vote is to take place today.
- President Guntis Ulmanis is in Germany, where he will visit the Hannover Messe trade fair, where Latvian producers are represented.
- Three major governing factions back changes in the parliament election law aimed at restricting the creation of new parties and preventing deputies moving between parties.

- The co-operation council of the governing factions listened to Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs to know why Latvia is behind the two other Baltic states in concluding visa-free agreements with European countries. Birkavs said the main reason was that Latvia has not yet acceded to the 1951 Geneva convention.
- The co-operation council agreed on proposing Olafs Bruveris from the Saimnieks Party as candidate to the post of director of the state bureau of human rights.
- Latvia's trade balance has changed in February to imports being 54.4 percent higher than exports, down from a 68.1 percent difference at the start of the year.
- Latvian farmers' incomes are likely to drop by 20.2 million lats, according to an angriculture ministry report.
- One of the five Latvian pilots arrested in India suffered a heart attack but the prison administration denied him special medical treatment.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele foresees 1997 inflation at 8.8 percent, he told the London Institute of Directors.
- As a result of three-stage privatisation of Ventspils Nafta, some 100,000 people may become shareholders of the company.
